name: Qwen3
notes: Don't use greedy decoding (temperature 0) in thinking mode: Qwen says it lowers quality and causes endless repetition.
If answers repeat endlessly, set presence_penalty to 1.5.
Add /think or /no_think to a message to switch thinking on or off for that turn.

name: Qwen3.5

lmstudio.note: In LM Studio, turn off KV cache quantization for this model: MLX vision models of this architecture fail to load with it.

notes: For precise coding in thinking mode, Qwen suggests temperature 0.6 and presence_penalty 0. For reasoning without thinking: temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, top_k 40, presence_penalty 2.0.
presence_penalty between 0 and 2 reduces endless repetition; high values can mix languages.
Keep at least 128K tokens of context so thinking works well.

name: Qwen3-VL
notes: Vision model: to send images, use mlx-vlm, mlx-openai-server, vllm-mlx or LM Studio. mlx-lm only reads text.

name: Qwen3.8
notes: reasoning_effort sets how long it thinks: low, medium or xhigh (the default). Lower effort is faster per answer but can need more retries in agent work.
preserve_thinking is on by default: earlier turns keep their reasoning, which costs tokens but helps multi-turn accuracy.
For agent work Qwen suggests long outputs: up to 262,144 tokens of reasoning and 131,072 tokens of answer.

If tool calls fail when a client sends arguments as JSON strings, or thinking runs out of tokens at xhigh, the community template froggeric/Qwen-Fixed-Chat-Templates fixes both (it defaults to medium effort). Replace chat_template.jinja in the model folder with it.

name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

omlx.note: Turn on native MTP in oMLX's model settings for MTP builds.

mlx-vlm.note: Needs an mlx-vlm with qwen4_exp support; older releases can't load it.

notes: The qwen4_exp architecture (n-gram embedding, hyper-connections, Qwen Sparse Attention) runs on mlx-serve 26.8.11 or newer, oMLX 0.6.4 or newer and recent mlx-vlm. mlx-lm and the engines built on it can't load it.
mlx-serve packs (with ngram_table.bin) run only on mlx-serve. Standard MLX builds run on mlx-vlm and oMLX.
Don't attach a Qwen3.8-27B MTP drafter: Flash-Next has different hidden sizes. MTP builds ship their own MTP block.

name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Uncensored, mlx-serve 4-bit pack
notes: Needs at least 96 GB of unified memory (128 GB recommended for long agent contexts); about 68 GB stays resident.
Keep it on the internal SSD: the 51B-parameter n-gram table (ngram_table.bin) is read from disk while it generates.
mlx-serve drafts with the model's MTP head for faster generation. For agent work, --reasoning-budget 2048 keeps thinking short.

name: Qwen3.8-27B Uncensored (orcarouter)

mlx-vlm.note: The MTP drafter is in the repo's mtp/ folder. mlx-vlm uses it with --draft-model <mtp folder> --draft-kind mtp --draft-block-size 4.

notes: Gated on Hugging Face: accept the terms on the model page, then add a read token in MLXRunner Settings to download it.
The repo root is the 4-bit build. Avoid the 2-bit build: it breaks down into repetition loops and garbled text.

name: Qwen3.6
notes: For precise coding in thinking mode, Qwen suggests temperature 0.6. For hard math and programming, allow up to 81,920 output tokens.
Qwen3.6 doesn't support the /think and /no_think soft switch; turn thinking off with enable_thinking false.
Earlier turns drop their reasoning unless you send preserve_thinking true, which helps agents reuse the KV cache.
Keep at least 128K tokens of context so thinking works well.

name: Gemma 4
notes: Thinking is off by default. Turn it on with enable_thinking true (or <|think|> at the start of the system prompt).
In multi-turn chats, keep only the final answers of earlier turns, not their thoughts, except in tool-call turns.
Vision model: send images before the text. E2B, E4B and 12B also take audio. To send images, use mlx-vlm, mlx-openai-server or LM Studio.
Context: 256K tokens.

name: Ornith 1.5
notes: Always reasons first, in a <think> block; the card gives no way to turn it off.
The card's benchmarks use temperature 1.0.
For about 1M tokens of context, YaRN factor 4.0 over 262,144 native tokens; only switch it on when you need it.

name: Bonsai 2 ternary
notes: Ternary Bonsai 2 packs load natively in mlx-vlm 0.7.8 or newer. mlx-lm 0.32.0 can't load them yet; no MLX fork is needed.

name: Bonsai 1-bit
notes: Needs PrismML's MLX fork with 1-bit kernels (pip install "mlx @ git+https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/mlx.git@prism"); upstream support is still pending. MLXRunner's engines use standard MLX.

name: JANG pack (vMLX)
notes: JANG packs carry a Hadamard sidecar that only vMLX applies. Standard MLX engines load them but produce garbage, so run it in vMLX.

name: Edge0
notes: Edge0 needs its own runtime (edge0 serve) to apply its LoRA and pre-router. MLXRunner's engines only run the base Qwen3.6 weights, which is not Edge0.
It streams experts from the SSD, so keep it on the internal SSD.

name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
notes: deepseek_v41 runs on mlx-serve 26.10.3 or newer (and oMLX's V4.1 port, not in its releases yet). Mainline mlx-vlm, mlx-lm and transformers can't load it.
Thinking is on by default; send enable_thinking false to turn it off. mlx-serve drafts with its DSpark MTP stages by default (--no-mtp or enable_mtp false turns them off).
Its Engram tables (about 200 GB) are read from the SSD for every token: keep it on the internal SSD.
Context: 1,048,576 tokens.

name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, mlx-serve pruned 2.25 bpw pack
notes: About 92 GB stays resident; made for 128 GB Macs. Download: 296 GB.
Half of the experts are pruned: chat quality drops and non-English text degrades badly. On a 256 GB Mac use the 3.0 bpw pack.

name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, mlx-serve 3.0 bpw pack
notes: About 209 GB stays resident and loading needs about 215 GB free: close large apps first. Download: 427 GB.

name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, mlx-serve iQ 4.7 bpw pack
notes: About 75 GB stays resident; 128 GB Mac recommended. The 32 GB ngram_table.bin is memory-mapped from the SSD.
MTP drafts by default; --no-mtp or enable_mtp false turns it off. --kv-quant 8 halves the KV cache.

name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, mlx-serve iQ 3.3 bpw pack
notes: Made for 64 GB Macs (about 52 GB resident). On a 64 GB Mac, run sudo sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb=58000 once after every restart, and add --skip-mem-preflight and --ctx-size 65536 in Extra engine arguments.
The first long prompt after a restart is slower while ngram_table.bin is read from the SSD.

name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, mlx-serve mixed 4/8-bit pack
notes: No longer updated: the author recommends the iQ-MLX-4.7bpw pack, same size and closer to the original.

name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Uncensored (orcarouter)
notes: The 4-bit build at the repo root needs 163 GB of memory (6-bit 192 GB, 8-bit 221 GB): Mac Studio Ultra class.
Gated on Hugging Face: accept the terms on the model page, then add a read token in MLXRunner Settings to download it.

name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next REAP-288

omlx.note: With a memory guard below 68 GB (omlx serve --memory-guard-gb 48), oMLX streams the n-gram table from the SSD and needs about 39 GB.

notes: Experts pruned from 512 to 288 for agentic coding: about 68 GB resident on mlx-vlm. Other domains and vision may lose more quality.

name: Qwen3.8-27B MTPLX Optimized Speed

mtplx.note: Built for MTPLX: no flags needed, it reads its tuned settings from mtplx_runtime.json.

notes: Peak memory about 23.6 GB. On M1 and M2 Macs the author recommends the FP16 build.

name: Qwen3.8-9B heretic MTPLX

mtplx.note: The author starts it with --mtp --depth 2 --profile sustained --verify-strategy capture_commit --verify-core linear-gdn-from-conv-tape --mtp-adapter <model folder>/mtp-adapter-r64.npz --merge-mtp-adapter. Add these in Extra engine arguments; depth 3 or more doesn't pay.

notes: Always opens with a <think> block, so leave room in the output length.

name: Solstice Qwen3.8-27B TURBO 1M
notes: The full 1M context needs 64 GB or more; 36 GB Macs manage up to 262K. The card's 3-bit TurboQuant KV cache and its Anvil runtime aren't available in MLXRunner's engines.
The card's benchmarks use temperature 1.0 and top_p 0.95.
